body_text: View all news Sable Offshore Corp. Prices Offerings of Common Stock and Convertible Senior Notes 07/01/2026 Download (opens in new window) HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Sable Offshore Corp. (New York Stock Exchange: SOC) today announced the pricing of its concurrent public offerings of 32,467,533 shares of common stock, at a public offering price of $3.08 per share, and $300.0 million aggregate principal amount of 6.5% convertible senior notes due 2031 (the “notes”). The issuance and sale of the common stock and the notes are scheduled to settle on July 2, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Sable also granted the underwriters of the common stock offering a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 4,870,129 shares of common stock solely to cover over-allotments, and granted the underwriters of the notes offering a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional $45.0 million aggregate principal amount of notes solely to cover over-allotments. J.P. Morgan is acting as sole book-running manager for the common stock offering and the notes offering. The notes will be senior, unsecured obligations of Sable and will accrue interest at a rate of 6.5% per annum, payable semi-annually in arrears on January 1 and July 1 of each year, beginning on January 1, 2027. The notes will mature on July 1, 2031, unless earlier repurchased, redeemed or converted. Before April 1, 2031, noteholders will have the right to convert their notes only upon the occurrence of certain events. From and after April 1, 2031, noteholders may convert their notes at any time at their election until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date. Sable will settle conversions by paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its common stock or a combination of cash and shares of its common stock, at Sable’s election. The initial conversion rate is 249.7502 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $4.00 per share of common stock. The initial conversion price represents a premium of approximately 30% over the public offering price per share of common stock in the common stock offering. The conversion rate and conversion price will be subject to adjustment upon the occurrence of certain events. The notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part (subject to certain limitations), for cash at Sable’s option at any time, and from time to time, on or after July 6, 2029 and on or before the 40th scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, but only if the last reported sale price per share of Sable’s common stock exceeds 175% of the conversion price for a specified period of time. The redemption price will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date. If a “fundamental change” (as defined in the indenture for the notes) occurs, then, subject to a limited exception, noteholders may require Sable to repurchase their notes for cash. The repurchase price will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the applicable repurchase date. In addition, noteholders may require Sable to repurchase their notes on July 6, 2029, at a cash repurchase price equal to the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the repurchase date. Sable estimates that the net proceeds from the common stock offering will be approximately $92.8 million (or approximately $107.0 million if the underwriters of the common stock offering fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares of common stock), after deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses. Sable estimates that the net proceeds from the notes offering will be approximately $288.8 million (or approximately $332.5 million if the underwriters of the notes offering fully exercise their option to purchase additional notes), after deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions and Sable’s estimated offering expenses. Sable intends to use the net proceeds from the common stock offering and the notes offering, together with the proceeds from the previously announced New Senior Secured Term Loan, to repay its Senior Secured Term Loan with Exxon Mobil Corporation, to pay transaction fees and expenses and for general corporate purposes. The New Senior Secured Term Loan, the common stock offering and the notes offering are cross conditioned, and accordingly each transaction will be consummated only if all such transactions are consummated. The offerings are being made pursuant to an effective shelf registration statement on file with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”). Each offering will be made only by means of a prospectus supplement relating to that offering (including any supplements thereto) and an accompanying prospectus. An electronic copy of the preliminary prospectus supplement (and, when available, the final prospectus supplement) for each offering, together with the accompanying prospectus, is or will be available on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov . Alternatively, copies of these documents can be obtained by contacting: J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, c/o Broadridge Financial Solutions, 1155 Long Island Avenue, Edgewood, New York 11717, by email at prospectus-eq_fi@jpmchase.com and postsalemanualrequests@broadridge.com . This press release does not constitute an offer to sell, or the solicitation of an offer to buy, any securities referred to in this press release, nor will there be any sale of any such securities, in any state or other jurisdiction in which such offer, sale or solicitation would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of such state or jurisdiction. About Sable Sable Offshore Corp. is an independent oil and gas company, headquartered in Houston, Texas, focused on responsibly developing the Santa Ynez Unit in federal waters offshore California. The Sable team has extensive experience safely operating in California. body_text: Scientists Receiving NIH Grants Nominated Fauci for Prestigious Awards, Emails Reveal Recently released emails made public by Sen. Rand Paul's office have renewed discussion about former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Director Dr. Anthony Fauci and the prestigious awards he received before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. The documents indicate that several scientists who had received substantial funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) nominated Fauci for high profile awards, raising fresh questions about potential conflicts of interest and government ethics. The emails, released on July 24 by the office of Sen. Rand Paul, chairman of the U.S. Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, have sparked debate over whether recipients of NIH funding should have participated in nominating the longtime public health official for lucrative international prizes. Emails Show Award Nominations from NIH Funded Scientists According to the released correspondence, Dr. Charles Dinarello, a professor of medicine and immunology at the University of Colorado School of Medicine, nominated Anthony Fauci for the Dan David Prize in 2020. The Dan David Prize is an internationally recognized award that, at the time, carried a total value of $1 million, with $900,000 awarded directly to the recipient. In one email, Dinarello stated that Fauci and his longtime aide, Greg Folkers, completed much of the work required for the nomination package. Fauci ultimately received the award. The emails also include congratulatory messages exchanged among colleagues after the ethics review was completed. One employee joked about Fauci becoming wealthy from the prize, while another humorously requested a percentage of the winnings. Ethics Review Cleared Acceptance of Prize Before Fauci accepted the Dan David Prize, government ethics officials reviewed whether accepting the award would violate constitutional restrictions regarding foreign gifts. According to the review, officials concluded that accepting the prize did not violate the U.S. Constitution because the Dan David Prize operates independently of Tel Aviv University, despite being based there. Officials determined that the foundation had sufficient independence to allow acceptance of the award. However, not everyone agreed with that conclusion. Former law professor E. Donald Elliott argued in a published opinion article that because Tel Aviv University receives significant financial support from the Israeli government, acceptance of the prize should have been considered unconstitutional under the Constitution's foreign emoluments provisions. The differing legal interpretations have remained part of the broader public discussion surrounding the award. Other Prize Money Was Restricted The released documents also reveal that ethics officials did not approve every prize opportunity presented to Fauci. In some cases, government ethics advisers determined that Fauci could not accept prize money from organizations that received funding from NIAID, the institute he led from 1984 until 2022. One example involved the Georgia Institute of Technology, where officials reportedly concluded that accepting prize funds would create an ethics concern because the institution was an NIH grant recipient. These decisions demonstrate that ethics reviews were conducted individually depending on the circumstances surrounding each award. Funding Records Draw Attention Public funding records indicate that Dr. Charles Dinarello received millions of dollars in research grants from NIAID over several decades, beginning in the mid 1980s. The records cited in the released documents show that additional NIH funding continued after Dinarello nominated Fauci for the Dan David Prize. While the timing has attracted public attention, the emails themselves do not provide evidence that funding decisions were directly connected to the award nominations. Fauci Also Discussed Other Award Nominations The released emails include additional exchanges involving other prestigious scientific awards. In 2021, Dinarello contacted Greg Folkers asking whether Fauci had been invited to nominate someone for the Shaw Prize. Fauci responded that if Dinarello wanted to be nominated, he would be willing to submit his name. Fauci also suggested that Dinarello prepare much of the nomination paperwork, similar to previous nominations. The correspondence illustrates the professional relationships that existed among prominent medical researchers involved in major scientific awards. Barton Haynes Also Nominated Fauci Another scientist mentioned in the emails is Dr. Barton Haynes, a professor of medicine at Duke University School of Medicine. According to the documents, Haynes nominated Fauci for multiple awards over several years, including the Dan David Prize and the Heinz Award for the Human Condition. One email indicates that Fauci personally asked Haynes to serve as his nominator for the Heinz Award. Fauci explained that Haynes would first need to register as an official nominator before the paperwork could be submitted. Haynes agreed and replied that he believed the award would be a good fit. Despite the nomination, Fauci did not receive either the Heinz Award or the Shaw Prize. NIH Funding to Haynes Also Highlighted Funding records referenced in the released materials indicate that Barton Haynes had received more than $100 million in NIAID research grants before one of Fauci's award nominations. Additional funding reportedly continued afterward. The documents have prompted questions from critics regarding whether researchers receiving federal grants should participate in award nominations involving senior agency officials. However, the released emails do not establish that grant funding was influenced by those nominations. Sen. Rand Paul Raises Questions Sen. Rand Paul said the newly released records raise concerns about the appearance of a possible conflict of interest. In a public statement accompanying the document release, Paul said the records raise questions about whether a quid pro quo may have existed given the significant financial value associated with some of the awards. Neither the NIH, Anthony Fauci, nor Barton Haynes responded to media requests for comment before the original report was published, according to the source article. Broader Public Discussion Continues The release of these emails has added another chapter to the ongoing public debate surrounding Anthony Fauci's leadership during his decades at NIAID and throughout the COVID 19 pandemic. Supporters argue that Fauci's awards reflected decades of scientific contributions and public service. Critics maintain that the relationships between grant recipients and agency leadership deserve closer examination to ensure transparency and maintain public confidence in government institutions. Whether additional investigations or reviews will follow remains uncertain, but the documents have generated renewed interest in federal ethics procedures and the nomination process for prestigious international awards. Conclusion The newly released emails reveal that several scientists who had received NIH funding nominated Anthony Fauci for major awards, including the million dollar Dan David Prize. While government ethics officials approved Fauci's acceptance of that award, the documents have fueled renewed debate about transparency, conflicts of interest, and the appearance of impartiality in federal agencies. As lawmakers continue reviewing the records, the discussion is likely to remain part of the broader conversation about public accountability, government ethics, and the relationships between federal research agencies and the scientists they support. Source: The Epoch Times and publicly released emails referenced by the office of Sen. Rand Paul. Disclaimer: This content is provided for informational and educational purposes only. It summarizes publicly reported information and allegations contained in released documents. The individuals and organizations mentioned may dispute interpretations of these records. Readers are encouraged to review official documents and statements for additional context.

title: Guía para limpiar los faros opacos de tu auto
summary: Aquí te explicamos cómo puedes limpiar los faros de tu auto y si lo necesitas, te mostramos cómo debes de pulirlos de forma sencilla y sin gastar de más.
body_text: ¿Has notados que los faros de tu auto ya no iluminan como antes? Si es tu caso quizás debas limpiarlos o pulirlos para mejorar la iluminación que brindan en el camino. En este artículo te contaremos dos métodos sencillos y muy efectivos para limpiar los faros de tu auto o bien, si es necesario, pulirlos sin tener que gastar de más. En primer lugar, ¿por qué se vuelven opacos los faros del auto? La mayoría de los faros modernos están hechos de un plástico rígido llamado policarbonato. Este material se oxida debido a la luz del sol y a los cambios de temperatura ocasionando el molesto color amarillento. Antes de limpiar los faros del auto Antes de comenzar la limpieza verifica que el faro no tenga cuarteaduras o esté roto , de ser así tal vez sea momento de cambiarlos. De la misma forma, revisa que no haya agua dentro del faro en cuyo caso será mejor retirarlo para secar el líquido. Por último asegúrate que las manchas amarillas estén del lado exterior del faro, de no ser así, no te preocupes los mismos proceso que te explicamos en este artículo sirve para limpiar y pulir el interior del faro . Limpiar faros amarillos con pasta de dientes Primero queremos hablarte de una forma muy común y bastantante accesible para limpiar los faros opacos de tu auto y es con pasta dental. Así es, el dentífrico usualmente contiene sodio y floruro, materiales no abrasivos que pueden desprenden la oxidación de los faros de tu auto. Este método es excelente si lo que quieres es retirar la oxidación del faro (que el faro se vea amarillo) pero si notas que está rayado, es mejor que lo pulas como te explicamos en el segundo punto. Lo primero será reunir los materiales que necesitaremos: Pasta dental común Toallas de papel Barniz transparente o cera para autos Líquido para limpiar cristales Cinta para enmascarar 1. Para limpiar los faros del auto , lo primero es cubrir la carrocería alrededor del mismo para evitar dañarla con la pasta de dientes, aún cuando no es abrasiva, si quedan residuos podrían afectar la pintura del auto. No es recomendable utilizar cinta de aislar o masking tape ya que al momento de retirarla podría arrancar la pintura de nuestro vehículo. Incluso, si te es más fácil puedes usar una bolsa de plástico para proteger el exterior del faro. 2. Una vez que hayamos protegido la carrocería alrededor del auto, lo siguiente será aplicar de forma abundante pasta dental sobre el faro del auto. 3. Con una toalla de papel la vamos a distribuir sobre todo el faro al mismo tiempo que frotamos de forma circular. Es recomendable que frotes durante cinco minutos. Si es necesario que apliques un poco más de pasta dental, no habrá problema; utiliza la cantidad necesaria para que cubra todo el faro. Debes notar como la pasta se torna amarilla por la oxidación que está quitando. 4. Después de limpiar lo amarillento el faro, utiliza el líquido para limpiar cristal para retirar la pasta de dientes restante. Con una toalla de papel limpia, retira los excesos para dejar el faro reluciente. 5. Por último, aplica el barniz o la cera para proteger el faro de la luz del sol y evitar que se oxide demasiado pronto. Este proceso lo puedes repetir las veces que sean necesaria para que obtengas las claridad deseada. Te dejamos un video que muestra cómo limpiar los faros de tu auto Te puede interesar: Cinco sencillas formas de cuidar el auto del sol Pulir los faros opacos del coche Si los faros de tu auto además están rayados , rayados lo mejor será que los pulas para mejorar su transparencia. ¿Qué necesitaremos? Líquido para aclarar faros Lijas número 200, 250 y 300 (lijas para pulir faros) Lubricante para faros Cera o barniz Cinta para enmascarar Trapos de tela Todos los materiales, se conocen como kit para limpiar faros del auto y lo puedes adquirir en cualquier ferretería o en una tienda de autoservicio. El precio es bastante accesible; alrededor de $300 pesos. 1 Para pulir los faros opacos de tu auto lo primero que debemos hacer es cubrir la chapa del auto para evitar dañar la pintura . Utiliza la cinta para enmascarar o bien una plástico que cubra la superficie que rodea al faro. No utilices cinta de aislar o masking tape. 2 Con un trapo esparce el líquido aclarador sobre el faro y talla durante tres minutos. Cubre el faro por completo y deja secar por al menos tres minutos más; pasado el tiempo retira el líquido con un trapo limpio. 3 Rocía el lubricante sobre el faro y talla con la lija de 200 de arriba hacia abajo. Si el lubricante se seca rocía un poco más. Retira los residuos con un trapo limpio. 4 El cuarto paso será aplicar de nueva cuenta el lubricante y lijar el faro pero ahora con la lija del 250 y con movimientos de lado a lado. Retira los residuos con un trapo. 5 El siguiente paso es el mismo que los dos anteriores pero ahora lijamos con la lija del número 300 alternando con movimientos de arriba a abajo y de lado a lado. De nueva cuenta es necesario que retires los residuos con un trapo. Cabe señalar que existen diferentes lijas, unas más ásperas y otras más suaves. Si quieres obtener mejores resultados puedes conseguir lijas más suaves y repetir el mismo proceso pero ahora las lijas más suaves. 6 Vuelve a aplicar el líquido aclarante y espárcelo sobre todo el faro. 7 Ahora sólo resta que apliques el barniz o la cera para faros para protegerlo lo más posible del sol. No te preocupes, si encuentras diferentes formas para limpiar y pulir los faros de tu auto, básicamente se trata de tallar los faros con lijas de diferente porosidad y aplicar selladores, barniz o cera para fijar el pulido. Por último, te compartimos el video donde se explica de forma gráfica el proceso antes mencionado. ¿Quieres comprar tu auto? , en Nexu te ofrecemos un esquema de arrendamiento personalizado para obtener el mayor beneficio fiscal. title: The income you need to buy a home in America’s biggest metros
summary: How much do you need to earn to buy a home in America's biggest metros? From nearly $480K in San Jose to under $65K in Pittsburgh, here is the income picture.
body_text: By Jason Bulloch, Offerpad Research Team Buying a home in San Jose, California, takes nearly $480,000 in annual income. In Pittsburgh, it is under $65,000. These are not minor differences. They point to a market fracturing along geographic lines, where location increasingly decides whether homeownership stays within reach. The housing market generates a lot of data on the annual salary needed to buy in the largest U.S. metro areas. The figures for this and the calculations below come from HSH , which combines statistics from the National Association of Realtors (NAR), major mortgage providers, and salary data from sources including the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) to give a quarter-by-quarter view of income requirements in major metros. Each figure assumes a 20% down payment and the traditional 28% debt-to-income ratio most lenders recommend, on a 30-year mortgage at 6.11% interest, a common rate in the market right now. Below, Offerpad , a real estate technology company, breaks down a few of these figures and what they mean for prospective homebuyers. New York City: $197,521.96 Buyers eyeing New York City need almost $200,000 a year to cover the $4,608.85 average monthly payment they can expect, with median property prices at $750,000. Prices in NYC are actually down slightly, by 0.48% compared with Q4 2025, though that is unlikely to offer much comfort to people in lower salary brackets. It also cements professional couples as among the best positioned to buy affordably. Los Angeles: $204,796.14 Across the country, the pattern mirrors NYC. Average monthly payments are higher, at $4,778.58, because median property prices in LA were $858,500 in Q1 2026, down 8.64% quarter over quarter. The modest easing of prices in some major metros like LA may be due in part to sluggish sales and longer days on market (DOM) early in the year, peaking at 68 DOM in January 2026, per data from FRED . When a market stalls, buyers can gain leverage, and sellers may look to speed up a sale by lowering the asking price or seeking cash buyers rather than mortgaged buyers. With LA’s price peak among the highest in the country, a dip like this is reasonably read as a correction rather than a long-term slide. Even people in high-paying tech and entertainment jobs across the city may still struggle to enter the market today. Chicago: $107,546.56 Covering a metro area of almost 10 million residents, Chicago looks a little better than NYC or LA on affordability. Median home prices sat at $384,100 in Q1 2026, with monthly payments on a typical 30-year mortgage estimated at $2,509.42. BLS data on average wages shows there is still an affordability gap. Mean hourly earnings in Chicago were $34.42 in 2024, the most recent year available, while the U.S. Census Bureau puts per-capita annual income at $50,086 and household income around $77,000. In other words, individuals, couples, or families earning a typical amount for the city cannot meet the lending requirements. Dallas: $105,798.75 Dallas is the first metro on this list where prices have risen on average so far in 2026, up 0.65% to a median of $369,000. With a 30-year mortgage locked in at the standard 6.11% rate, buyers pay $2,468.64 a month, as long as they can also come up with the 20% down payment. Median household income here is roughly on par with Chicago, at $70,518 . Individuals earn around $45,000 on average, so there is the same gap between what people take home and what the current market asks of new buyers. The national picture Nationally, the average income needed to enter affordable homeownership is $103,419.69, reflecting a current median home price of $404,300. That lines up with metros like Chicago and Dallas, and it is about half what NYC and LA require. There are outliers at both ends. San Jose’s $477,409.52 income requirement, tied to a median price above $2 million, sits at the top. At the other end, an average Pittsburgh home is within reach for someone earning $62,891.16, the lowest income bar of any of the top 50 metros. Softening in some regions may point to better affordability ahead. But if those price drops are tied to broader economic strain and rising interest rates, many buyers still will not have the income to meet even lower requirements. While price moderation in select metros offers marginal relief, rising interest rates and income thresholds keep buying out of reach across many major markets. The gap between typical incomes and financing requirements remains the main affordability barrier. This story was produced by Offerpad and reviewed and distributed by Stacker .

title: Cracking the code on maritime carbon capture
body_text: To complete the installation, we moved the Seabound team to a shipyard in Yalova, Turkey, where the Sounion Trader was undergoing routine maintenance. Over the course of several weeks, we collaborated with the shipyard and the ship’s crew to install our equipment and connect it to one of the ship’s auxiliary engines. We also worked with the American Bureau of Shipping and Lloyd’s Register to gain approval for operating the system onboard and to conduct a detailed risk assessment, respectively. When the ship set sail for the Middle East, we joined the crew for two months, taking turns to run numerous carbon capture trials and gain hands-on experience operating at sea. With each test, we managed to increase the carbon capture rate, culminating in 78% efficiency and ~1 ton of CO2 captured per day.
